recommendation: Keep this audit commit and ask FHIR-I to decide whether history Bundle entries may use entry.request.method PATCH. If yes, revise bdl-14 and the HTTP history text; if no, remove PATCH from the Bundle history resource-inclusion sentence and bdl-3b history expression while leaving PATCH allowed for transaction and batch Bundles.
issue_request: FHIR-19620 is Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked the HTTP history documentation to clarify that PATCH creates a history entry, that the resulting history Bundle represents PATCH as PUT, and that PATCH cannot be used when Bundle.type is history.
initial_application: Git commit 3dff2e6f876c7cdbdbed773ad35b754a74fa729e explicitly applied the issue by updating source/http.html and adding Bundle invariant bdl-14. Current source/http.html still says PATCH interactions are represented as PUT in history, and current source/bundle/structuredefinition-Bundle.xml still contains bdl-14 prohibiting PATCH in history Bundles.
additional_context: The Bundle resource is active in source/fhir.ini. Current source/bundle/bundle-notes.xml and bdl-3b still mention PATCH for history resource inclusion because FHIR-34388, a later Published/Persuasive issue, requested that wording. FHIR-34388 already has a combined-branch human-review audit commit because choosing between PATCH-as-PUT and PATCH-as-history-method requires FHIR-I review. FHIR-50118 later reports a bdl-3b mismatch but is Triaged and unresolved.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Removing PATCH from Bundle history narrative and bdl-3b would effectively reverse another final Jira decision, while revising bdl-14/HTTP would reverse FHIR-19620. The safe reconciliation is a durable human-review audit for the seed.
